scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.

The 1715 and 1815 snapshots for the two Montserrat records were decoded and their footprints checked: both cover the same island, approximately longitude -62.236 to -62.138, latitude 16.672 to 16.811. Shared narrative does not certify exact polygons or imply the coverage intervals are lifetimes.

Brown’s archaeological chronology and the specialist Trants account are preferred over the tourism page’s claim of a first Taino settlement in 500 BCE. Indentured Irish labour is not equated with African chattel slavery. Colonial occupations interrupt the longer plantation phase.

DAACS separates the cattle mill’s original function from later sedimentation and notes missing excavation records. The workers’ village has eroded, and many vessel forms are tentative. No complete household, recipe or sanitation system is invented.
The AIA school programme is the completed July 2012 season. It is distinguished from later 2013 projects and plans for future seasons.
Goat-water descriptions are paraphrased as a food and social custom. Recipes and music lyrics are not reproduced, and uncertain claims about official sporting anthems are omitted.

MVO direct pages returned intermittent errors; their indexed full text supplied the cited history and monitoring passages. Plymouth evacuation in 1996 is distinguished from destructive flows in 1997. The 2003 observatory move is not assigned a month because institutional pages differ.
Current danger zones and access rules are not described as historical constants. No safety prediction, exact future eruption claim or visitor advice is made.

Constitution commencement and territory status were checked in the Government of Montserrat’s indexed page. Source lists and this evidence packet are not independent historical or geometry certification.

sharedAssociations.basis: Repeated footprints cover Montserrat in separate snapshot intervals. The shared island account distinguishes political changes, evacuation and cultural continuity.
